title: LA to Las Vegas
summary: The desert run everyone makes. Charging is dense now, but the big sites cluster, and Baker on a Sunday afternoon is still Baker.
startNote: Mileage starts where most LA drivers join I-15: the I-10 junction at exit 109.

originLegs.note: Estimate. Driving distance from Los Angeles City Hall to the I-10 and I-15 junction.

stats.label: I-10 junction to Tropicana Ave
stats.note: From exit mileposts: CA exit 109 to the state line at mile 295.4, plus NV exit 37.

stops.name: Victor Valley
stops.why: First real stop after the Cajon Pass climb, and the last big town before open desert. Good place to top off if you left LA low.

price.value: Shown in the EA app and on the charger. EA does not publish it on the locator.

driverReports.summary: Busy town and a busy Walmart. Getting in and getting out might take some time on a busy day. Charger availability and reliability seems to be good, but I will skip this and consider other chargers if possible.
You have to go the wrong way in the lane to back in.

backups.name: Cardenas Market Hesperia
backups.facts: 4 chargers, 2 CCS cables each (8 cables). 350 kW per charger, shared when both cables are in use.

driverReports.summary: EA chargers at the Walmart down the road full as usual but most of the plugs here were available
Easy. No one here when I arrived. Quick to connect.
Painfully slow, maybe CA limits power when it's hot out?

backups.name: Green Tree Inn
backups.facts: 6 chargers. Four at 350 kW with two cables each, one of them with NACS cables; two cars on one charger share its power. Two at 100 kW with CCS and CHAdeMO.
backups.access: Open to all. NACS cables on one charger.

driverReports.summary: Easy payment with the Ford app and BlueOval Charge Network.

I love the charging options here and the best part, they are across the street from multiple restaurants and a coffee shop with a nice lounge area. Ignore the parking lot these are in, its actually peaceful here.
Was only giving 32 kW of charging. Couldn't wait. There's another and a father one at Cardenas Market. They're 350s. In use

backups.access: Open to all EVs. Non-Tesla CCS cars need a NACS adapter.

backups.facts: 20 stalls, up to 325 kW. Non-Tesla price varies by time of day; check the Tesla app.

backups.name: P66 / 76 Victorville

driverReports.summary: This might be the best charging station I've ever used. I've been here about a dozen times over the past year. I've never had any trouble of any kind. I've never had to wait, and it always delivers the max speed my vehicle will take.
$.64 per kilowatt hour on a Saturday afternoon with Chargers open. 76 gas station badging but Electrify America under the hood.
Nice quick stop. Convenience store location with a restroom.

stops.name: Barstow
stops.why: The main event. The most stalls on the corridor, with a CCS option and the outlets for a longer break.

access.value: Open to all EVs. Non-Tesla CCS cars need a NACS adapter. Trailer friendly.

price.value: Non-Tesla: $0.64/kWh, congestion fee up to $0.50/min. Tesla and members pay less.

driverReports.summary: Nice to have the longer V4 cables for my Lightning.
At the 120-stall Barstow site, the pull-through towing stall now has a sign, and a tire air station was added next to it.
Describes the 120-stall Barstow site as having solar canopies, V4 posts, and pull-through trailer stalls next to the highway.

backups.name: Walmart Barstow
backups.facts: 8 stalls: 7 at 350 kW CCS, 1 at 150 kW CCS with a 50 kW CHAdeMO. In the center of the Walmart lot near Home and Pharmacy.

driverReports.summary: Worked great. This station is very busy. I was lucky to not have to wait this time. A line formed while I was charging.
Works well. Not too busy. 25kW delivered in 20 mins.

At an Electrify America station in Barstow, a transit bus held a charger for about 1 hour 20 minutes while cars waited to charge. Walmart is the only EA site in Barstow in our data, so this is probably that site, but the post doesn't name it.

backups.access: Open to all EVs. Non-Tesla CCS cars need a NACS adapter.

driverReports.summary: Says the Barstow Outlets Supercharger was handing out $10 gift cards to spend at the outlets while charging.

backups.facts: Rivian's charging map lists 6 chargers, up to 300 kW, at 2835 Lenwood Rd, Barstow. Open to non-Rivian EVs. DOE lists the same port count.

driverReports.summary: At the Rivian Adventure Network site in Barstow, pulled a steady 148 kW for about 15 minutes. Lots of restaurants nearby.
Says the Barstow RAN chargers were replaced with v1.5 units and non-Rivian EVs can charge now. Saw a Kia, a Polestar, and a BMW charging.
Derated charging. Pulling ~60ish kw from an older dispenser.

reports.text: Sunday stop coming back from Vegas: mostly empty, but cable position was awkward for a Cybertruck. Older report.

around.text: Tanger Way site sits at the Outlets at Barstow.

driverReports.summary: Good location, chargers are older 150kw units. Got 70 max during the session because it was full.
Pedestal 8A 8b reported OUT OF SERVICE
Says the current Eddie World chargers top out at 72 kW.
Says charging in Yermo is poor on the old V2 stalls, but Eddie World itself is good.
Sometimes sees lines at the Eddie World Superchargers, usually a 10 to 15 minute wait at most.
Says Eddie World was the only Supercharger site they've used with a restroom that wasn't in an unrelated business nearby.

stops.name: Baker
stops.why: Last stop before the climb to Mountain Pass and the Nevada line. Busy on holiday and Sunday traffic, so have a backup in mind.

access.value: Open to all CCS EVs. Western part of the lot.

price.value: Shown in the EA app and on the charger. EA does not publish it on the locator.

driverReports.summary: Fast charge, appreciated the covered shade. Another charger here has a dead screen

If you pull in and there's empty chargers give your fellow EV driver a break and don't pick the plug adjacent to them because the load management immediately cuts the output in half. True here and basically everywhere.
Works well. Getting an average of 75kW. Charged from 44% to 75% in 25 mins. *note: Charge station 8 is down. No display.
Every stall at Electrify America Baker was taken. In 2021 they had been the only car there.
Every stall at Electrify America Baker was taken again; hopes the site gets expanded.
Electrify America Baker filled up right after they took the photo.
A Nissan Leaf driver in Baker couldn't find a working CHAdeMO charger. The poster notes that Electrify America in Baker is CCS only.

Says rolling blackouts shut down both Baker Supercharger sites that day, so they were rerouted. Applies to the Mojave Pointe Road site too.

Open to non-Teslas, next to an Arby's and a food court, clean restrooms. Had been offline for a couple of weeks at the time.

tips.text: Northbound, Baker to the state line includes the climb to Mountain Pass, the route's high point at 4,730 ft. Leave Baker with more than the distance alone suggests.

Non-Tesla drivers: four of the open Superchargers on this route are big enough to skip a queue (Barstow East Main at 120 stalls, Barstow Tanger Way at 70, Jean at 64, Baker Mojave Pointe at 40). You need your own NACS adapter.
Tesla-only sites on this route: Baker (Shell), Primm, Barstow Holiday Inn, Victorville Victor Plaza, and Yermo EddieWorld. Don't plan around them in a non-Tesla.
Every EA site on this guide had at least one charger down in May 2026 driver reports. Count on fewer stalls than listed.

arrival: Las Vegas arrival charging is not in this guide yet. It is next on the verification list. Lodging with chargers is also coming in the next update.
